newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baer buys remaining stake in Geneva unit.
newsitem.headline: Baer buys remaining stake in Geneva unit.

text.p: Swiss bank Julius Baer Holding AG said it had acquired the remaining 25 percent of the share capital of Societe Bancaire Julius Baer SA Geneve, held by the Lawi-Kadoorie Group.
As a wholly-owned subsidiary, the bank will change its name to Banque Julius Baer (Geneve) SA, Baer said in a statement.
Founded in 1934, the bank with assets under management of more than four billion Swiss francs, has some 140 employees and equity capital of 80 million francs.
Solly Lawi and Solly Alain Lawi, who were active at board and management levels, will form their own independent asset management company, Mirelis InvesTrust SA in Geneva.
